articles.title: PostgreSQL vs Firebase: Choosing Your App's Database
articles.excerpt: You are planning an app, and sooner or later someone asks the question that shapes everything else: where does the data live? If you have narrowed it down to two names, you are probably weighing Postg…
articles.body: You are planning an app, and sooner or later someone asks the question that shapes everything else: where does the data live? If you have narrowed it down to two names, you are probably weighing PostgreSQL vs Firebase . This guide lays out what each option actually is, where each one earns its keep, and the trade-offs that only show up months after launch, so you can choose with your eyes open. Here is the short version, up front: PostgreSQL is a relational database you control in detail. Firebase is a managed platform that bundles a database with authentication, hosting, and realtime sync. Neither is better in the abstract. The right choice depends on what your app does, how it will grow, and how much operational work your team wants to own.

articles.title: Rate Limits Are Not a Security Control: Why Business Logic Bugs Survive Every Scanner
articles.excerpt: A team I worked with had a textbook rate limiter. Twenty requests per minute per user, sliding window, Redis-backed, the works. Their scanner reported clean, their load tests looked fine, and their WA…
articles.body: A team I worked with had a textbook rate limiter. Twenty requests per minute per user, sliding window, Redis-backed, the works. Their scanner reported clean, their load tests looked fine, and their WAF dashboard was a flat green line. Then someone applied the same welcome coupon forty-seven times. Not in a minute. Over four days, one request at a time, well under every threshold. The limiter was doing exactly what it was configured to do. It was counting requests, and the attack was never about the number of requests. This is the shape of most business logic bugs: every individual request is legitimate, authorized, well-formed, and inside every quota. The vulnerability only exists in the sequence .

articles.title: I tried five agents to write one prompt. One agent did as well.
articles.excerpt: Nothing fancy: it is just one skill file that writes a prompt, or improves one, and attacks it before I use it. But I used it as an excuse to run a few experiments of my own on AI-assisted prompt writ…
articles.body: Nothing fancy: it is just one skill file that writes a prompt, or improves one, and attacks it before I use it. But I used it as an excuse to run a few experiments of my own on AI-assisted prompt writing. The main result: five agents did not write better prompts than one. The rules a prompt leaves out break it more often than its wording: how to verify a customer, who approves an exception, what to do when the input says to ignore the instructions. So the tool asks about them before it writes. Five agents against one Five agents to write one prompt is overkill, I know. Nobody would run that for real. It was a test: would more agents write a better prompt, or a worse one? I had a guess, but I wanted numbers. The pipeline cost 3.81 to 5.52 USD and 15 to 23 minutes per prompt.

articles.title: 39 Years Later, Calvin And Hobbes' Best Quote On Grief Is Still a Heartbreaking Classic
articles.excerpt: There's a lot more punch in this punchline than your usual Calvin and Hobbes comic strip
articles.body: Most of the time, Bill Watterson's Calvin and Hobbes was a straightforward comedy, set in equal parts a nondescript American suburb and its protagonist's imagination. While it's got more than its share of memorable lines and genuine wisdom, C&H was rarely out to tug on anyone's heartstrings. There are two exceptions to that rule. One is a full story arc from March 1987, in which Calvin tries to rescue a baby raccoon. The other is a one-shot from late in the comic's run, as one of Watterson's more experimental Sunday strips. Both are quiet meditations on death, as Calvin confronts mortality through encounters with animals.

articles.title: New Android exploit only needs you to install an app to wreck your phone
articles.excerpt: Android sabotages itself next.
articles.body: TL;DR Bitdefender researchers discovered an Android vulnerability that can trigger an endless crash loop simply by installing a specially crafted APK, potentially leaving devices unusable. The flaw exploits how Android handles ZIP compression methods, repeatedly crashing the core system_server process. Recovering may require a factory reset or manually deleting the malicious file using ADB. No in-the-wild exploitation has been identified, but the public disclosure could make it easier for threat actors to develop an exploit. Even though Android is a relatively safe operating system, with several security measures in place , threat actors’ ingenuity still keeps finding ways to exploit weaknesses.

articles.body: Credit: Oliver Cragg / Android Authority TL;DR We’ve seen the first Nintendo Switch 2 emulators on Android, although many games aren’t playable. We’ve also seen the BananaNative project, which enabled native ports of Donkey Kong Bananza and Mario Kart World on Android. It’s still early days for these projects, but it’s clear that Switch 2 emulation and native ports are progressing incredibly quickly. The Nintendo Switch 2 launched just over a year ago, but we weren’t expecting to see emulators or native ports on Android for a while yet. However, that’s exactly what’s happened in recent weeks. articles.body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is framed as a legend retold. For Zelda producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, a desire to pass the original game down to a younger group of Zelda developers is one of the main reasons this remake exists: “There are much younger developers who are working on this game, and I do think this is a really valuable experience for them to familiarize themselves first with the original Ocarina of Time and then have their own reinterpretation of it,” Aonuma said.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Full English Voice Cast Revealed
articles.excerpt: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is out now, and so we have confirmation of the full English voice cast for the first time.
articles.body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is out now, and so we have confirmation of the full English voice cast for the first time. As fans had suspected following the release of official trailers for the game, Matthew Mercer from the Dungeons & Dragons web series Critical Role, reprises his role as Ganondorf from The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. Prolific voice actor Erica Mendez plays Zelda, and Navi is voiced by Lisa Reimold. While the original Ocarina of Time, released in 1998 on the N64, did not feature any voiced dialogue, the remake features voice acting in its cutscenes. Link, of course, remains silent throughout — as he does in all the Zelda games. The full list, which IGN has verified via the credits, is below.

With a story spanning multiple time periods, Heat 2 serves as both a prequel and a sequel to the original film, and Driver's Wardell character is its principal antagonist. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 4, 2015: A rail-launched Super Strypi rocket carrying 13 baby satellites failed during its debut launch for the US Air Force
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force launched an experimental Super Strypi rail-launched rocket carrying 13 tiny satellites, but it failed just after liftoff from Hawaii.
articles.body: On Nov. 4, 2015, the United States Air Force planned to launch an experimental rocket for small satellites from the Pacific Missile Range Facility off Barking Sands, Kauai, Hawaii. The launch didn't according to plan . For this mission, the Air Force was testing out the Super Strypi rocket . The rocket used a rail to help with the liftoff. Super Strypi left the ground, but the rocket quickly spun out of control. When it crashed, it destroyed all of the tiny satellites riding aboard the rocket. The cause? Likely a problem with the first stage motor. The mission lost 13 tiny satellites known as cubesats. Cubesats are a popular option for space missions, because they are small and cheap, and they often operate in swarms.

articles.title: Hackers exploited iOS and Android flaws to infect phones
articles.excerpt: Researchers say group may have been Kremlin-sponsored in search of diplomatic targets.
articles.body: Hackers possibly linked to the Kremlin exploited previously patched iOS and Android flaws in an attempt to hack visitors of multiple websites, including one celebrating the 250th anniversary of American independence, researchers said Wednesday. The attackers, which the researchers assessed with “moderate to high confidence” were part of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service, targeted other sites, many with links to that country’s ongoing war against Ukraine. The attacks began when iPhone or Android users visited one of potentially hundreds of different sites. JavaScript injected into the traffic then profiled the device. The final payloads, tailored to the type of platform visiting, attempted to steal browser cookies and, in some cases, Wi-Fi passwords and full mobile device data.
